gloss: to make angry; to anger; to provoke

definitions.gloss: to make angry; to anger; to provoke; to upset
definitions.explanation: To cause someone to become angry through one's words or actions. The causative form of {怒|おこ}る (to get angry), used as a standard transitive verb.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}を{怒|おこ}らせてしまった。
examples.english: I ended up making her angry.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}を{怒|おこ}らせないほうがいい。
examples.english: You'd better not anger the teacher.

examples.japanese: {約束|やくそく}を{破|やぶ}って{友達|ともだち}を{怒|おこ}らせてしまい、{深|ふか}く{反省|はんせい}した。
examples.english: I broke a promise and made my friend angry, and I deeply regretted it.

notes:
The causative form of {怒|おこ}る (to get angry). Very commonly used in everyday conversation, especially with ～てしまう to express that one unintentionally made someone angry.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- （{人|ひと}）を{怒|おこ}らせる — to make someone angry
- {怒|おこ}らせてしまった — ended up making (someone) angry (unintentional)
- {怒|おこ}らせないように — so as not to anger (someone)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {怒|おこ}る — to get angry (intransitive base verb)
- {腹|はら}を{立|た}てさせる — to make someone upset (slightly more formal)
- {機嫌|きげん}を{損|そこ}ねる — to offend, to put in a bad mood (more indirect/subtle)
- {激怒|げきど}させる — to enrage (much stronger)
